programme.title: The Industrial Revolution - The Textile Industry
programme.desc: Turning to the actual process of industrialization that begins in the textile business; surveying the work of spinning and weaving textiles; learning about several key inventors; their innovations, such as the flying shuttle and the spinning jenny.

programme.title: The Industrial Revolution - Coal Mining
programme.desc: Coal mining becomes a large-scale capitalist enterprise; diving into one of the most dangerous jobs in the world; the problems miners have to overcome; examining some of the solutions; learning about steam engines, safety lamps, ventilation and more.

programme.title: The Industrial Revolution - Iron - Coking and Puddling
programme.desc: Iron is an important raw material for the Industrial Revolution; the history of iron; how to produce pig iron and forge wrought iron; meeting many of the key innovators who improve the process of bringing higher-quality iron into a growing market.

programme.title: The Middle East in the 20th Century - A Middle East Crossroads in the Year 1900
programme.desc: How western imperialism, the politics of oil, and the push for a Jewish state all set the stage for the 20th century.

programme.title: The Middle East in the 20th Century - Constitutional Revolts in Persia and Turkey
programme.desc: How protests in Persia led to a new government; then why the Young Turks wanted a united Turkey to supersede the Ottoman Empire.

programme.title: The Middle East in the 20th Century - World War I and the Ottoman Empire's Fall
programme.desc: The promises of Arab and Turkish nationalism and the construction of a Jewish state collide after the war.

programme.title: The Middle East in the 20th Century - Egyptian Revolution and Turkish Independence
programme.desc: The fallout from World War I with a look at the Turkish War of Independence in 1919, as well as anti-British uprisings from Egypt to Iraq.

programme.title: The Middle East in the 20th Century - Monarchies of the 20th-Century Middle East
programme.desc: Exploring the monarchies in the Middle East and North Africa in the period between the World Wars.

programme.title: The Middle East in the 20th Century - The Muslim Brotherhood and Its Founder
programme.desc: Imam Hassan al-Banna is the founder of the Muslim Brotherhood.

programme.title: The Middle East in the 20th Century - World War II Fault Lines in the Middle East
programme.desc: A high-level look at World War II and its impact on the Middle East and North Africa.

programme.title: The Middle East in the 20th Century - European Anti-Semitism and Israel's Birth
programme.desc: Tracing the development of Israel up to the creation of the state in 1948.

programme.title: The Industrial Revolution - Industrialization Is Good for You
programme.desc: Stepping into the story of one of the greatest periods in history; investigating why people should be grateful for the Industrial Revolution, even though there is much to dislike about industrialization.

programme.title: The Industrial Revolution - Why Was Britain First?
programme.desc: Starting at the beginning in the British Isles; various factors contribute to the birth of the Industrial Revolution, including relative political stability, sophisticated financial institutions, colonial trade and a rising population of workers.

programme.title: Miracle
programme.desc: When college coach Herb Brooks (Kurt Russell) is hired to helm the 1980 U.S. men's Olympic hockey team, he brings a unique and brash style to the ice. After assembling a team of hot-headed college all-stars, who are humiliated in an early match, Brooks unites his squad against a common foe, the heavily-favored Soviet team. As the U.S. squad tries to overcome insurmountable odds and win the gold medal, the team becomes a microcosm for American patriotism during the Cold War.

programme.title: Meet Me in St. Louis
programme.desc: "Meet Me in St. Louis" is a classic MGM romantic musical comedy that focuses on four sisters (one of whom is the nonpareil Judy Garland) on the cusp of the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair. The film spotlights the sisters' education in the ways of the world, which includes, but isn't limited to, learning about life and love, courtesy of the prototypical boy next door. In the end, love -- accompanied by song, dance and period costumes, all in glorious Technicolor -- conquers all.

programme.title: The Wizard of Oz
programme.desc: When a tornado rips through Kansas, Dorothy and her dog, Toto, are whisked away in their house to the magical land of Oz. They follow the Yellow Brick Road toward the Emerald City to meet the Wizard, and en route they meet a Scarecrow that needs a brain, a Tin Man missing a heart, and a Cowardly Lion who wants courage. The wizard asks the group to bring him the broom of the Wicked Witch of the West to earn his help.

programme.title: The Four Seasons
programme.desc: Jack (Alan Alda) and Kate (Carol Burnett) traditionally go on vacation with their friends every new season. Old friend Nick (Len Cariou) surprises everyone when he arrives not with his wife, Anne (Sandy Dennis), but with his new girlfriend, the much younger Ginny (Bess Armstrong). The group -- all of which had grown to be good friends with Anne -- must come to terms with this unexpected development. Ultimately, they learn to accept Nick's decision, and work to welcome Ginny as a friend.

programme.title: Annie
programme.desc: An orphan in a facility run by the mean Miss Hannigan, Annie believes that her parents left her there by mistake. When a rich man named Oliver "Daddy" Warbucks decides to let an orphan live at his home to promote his image, Annie is selected. While Annie gets accustomed to living in Warbucks' mansion, she still longs to meet her parents. So Warbucks announces a search for them and a reward, which brings out many frauds.

programme.title: Who's Been Sleeping in My Bed?
programme.desc: Jason Steel (Dean Martin) plays a wise, confident and handsome doctor on television — but besides the handsome part, that's where the comparisons end. In real life, Jason is scatterbrained and unsure about his impending marriage to Melissa (Elizabeth Montgomery), a gorgeous art teacher who most men would kill for. However, he may get a little sage advice of his own when he finds himself the de facto consultant for a group of married women who confuse his screen persona with reality.

programme.title: My Fair Lady
programme.desc: In this beloved musical, pompous phonetics professor Henry Higgins (Rex Harrison) is so sure of his abilities that he takes it upon himself to transform a Cockney working-class girl into someone who can pass for a cultured member of high society. His subject turns out to be the lovely Eliza Doolittle (Audrey Hepburn), who agrees to speech lessons to improve her job prospects. Higgins and Eliza clash, then form an unlikely bond -- one that is threatened by an aristocratic suitor (Jeremy Brett).

programme.title: Lili
programme.desc: Traveling with little more than her naïveté, sunny teenager Lili (Leslie Caron) arrives in a new town and is befriended by a circus troupe. Though she becomes infatuated with the dashing magician, Marcus the Magnificent (Jean-Pierre Aumont), Lili forms a more significant bond with puppeteer Paul (Mel Ferrer) and his four puppets, which she treats as real people. Together, Lili, Paul and the puppets prove to be a popular act, but their success and happiness are threatened by Paul's gruffness.

programme.title: Andy Hardy Meets Debutante
programme.desc: Young Andy Hardy (Mickey Rooney) journeys to New York with his father (Lewis Stone) and close friend Betsy Booth (Judy Garland), where he meets beautiful blonde socialite Daphne (Diana Lewis). Andy immediately forgets about Polly Benedict (Ann Rutherford), his girlfriend back home, and falls head over heels for Daphne. But as he starts to rub elbows with trendy Manhattanites, he begins to long for Polly -- and he soon realizes that the big city lacks the charms of his small hometown.

Lorsque des difficultés financières frappent sa famille et son église, George recule sur le ring et regagne le championnat à 45 ans, devenant ainsi le plus ancien champion poids lourd de l'histoire de la boxe.

programme.title: Young Sheldon
programme.desc: For young Sheldon Cooper, it isn't easy growing up in East Texas. Being a once-in-a-generation mind capable of advanced mathematics and science isn't always helpful in a land where church and football are king. And while the vulnerable, gifted and somewhat naive Sheldon deals with the world, his very normal family must find a way to deal with him. His father, George, is struggling to find his way as a high school football coach and as father to a boy he doesn't understand. Sheldon's mother, Mary, fiercely protects and nurtures her son. For 12 years on "The Big Bang Theory," audiences came to know the iconic, eccentric and extraordinary Sheldon Cooper. In "Young Sheldon," audiences get a chance to meet him in childhood, as he embarks on his innocent, awkward and hopeful journey toward the man he will become. Jim Parsons, who plays the adult version of Sheldon on "The Big Bang Theory," narrates.

programme.title: Young Sheldon
programme.desc: For young Sheldon Cooper, it isn't easy growing up in East Texas. Being a once-in-a-generation mind capable of advanced mathematics and science isn't always helpful in a land where church and football are king. And while the vulnerable, gifted and somewhat naive Sheldon deals with the world, his very normal family must find a way to deal with him. His father, George, is struggling to find his way as a high school football coach and as father to a boy he doesn't understand. Sheldon's mother, Mary, fiercely protects and nurtures her son. For 12 years on "The Big Bang Theory," audiences came to know the iconic, eccentric and extraordinary Sheldon Cooper. In "Young Sheldon," audiences get a chance to meet him in childhood, as he embarks on his innocent, awkward and hopeful journey toward the man he will become. Jim Parsons, who plays the adult version of Sheldon on "The Big Bang Theory," narrates.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: S1 East Lothian - Saving the Musselburgh Carriage Will Kirk and Kirsten Ramsay head to Musselburgh, on Scotland's east coast. It's a town boasting a proud heritage that is celebrated each year with a procession led by their elected Honest Lad and Honest Lass. However, for the past few years, the antique carriage these local luminaries ride in has been off the road. Restoring the carriage is a huge job that requires the skills of local signwriter Ross Hastie and wheelwright Greg Rowland, and made more complicated by the impending deadline of this year's festival. A musical instrument also needs some tender loving care and Will gets a makeover at Scotland's oldest bespoke tailors.
